channel.title: Cadence 步频 — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 50 sources.

item.title: The Optimal Exercise Modality and Dose for Blood Pressure Management in Middle-Aged and Older Adults: A Systematic Review with Bayesian Model-Based, and Dose-Response Network Meta-Analysis of RCTs.
item.description: A Bayesian network meta-analysis of RCTs evaluated the optimal exercise modality and dose for blood pressure management in middle-aged and older adults, systematically comparing effects across aerobic, resistance, and combined training.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of Telerehabilitation Versus Conventional Rehabilitation on Motor Function and Activities of Daily Living After Stroke: A Systematic Review of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review of four RCTs (N=226) found telerehabilitation to be non-inferior to conventional physiotherapy for improving motor function (Fugl-Meyer Assessment) and activities of daily living (Barthel Index) in stroke patients.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Comparative Efficacy of Body Acupuncture, Electroacupuncture, and Auricular Acupuncture in Stroke Rehabilitation: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trials.
item.description: A systematic review of 21 RCTs found acupuncture significantly improved motor function in stroke survivors (SMD=6.48; 95% CI=4.72-8.24; P<0.001), with electroacupuncture showing the greatest benefit.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness and feasibility of home-based physical exercise interventions for children and adolescents with chronic diseases: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis synthesized evidence on the effectiveness and feasibility of home-based physical exercise interventions for children and adolescents with chronic diseases, finding improvements in aerobic capacity, functional capacity, muscle strength, and quality of life.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Beyond the Diagnosis: An Integrated Perspective on Strategic Dosing in Neurologic Motor Rehabilitation. A Scoping Review and Collaborative Viewpoint.
item.description: A scoping review synthesizing 42 studies identified a clinical need for a mechanism-based framework to guide therapeutic reasoning and dosing in neurorehabilitation, supporting broad distinctions between higher-intensity approaches for non-progressive conditions and conservative strategies for progressive conditions.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effectiveness of a Personalized Robot-Assisted Trunk and Lower Limb Rehabilitation in Patients with Chronic Stroke: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: This RCT with 40 chronic stroke patients found that 3 months of personalized robot-assisted trunk and lower limb training, combined with conventional rehabilitation, significantly improved Functional Ambulatory Category (FAC) compared to conventional rehabilitation alone.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise Interventions for Older Adults with Alzheimer's Disease: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 142 articles explored the effectiveness and optimal dosage of physical exercise on cognitive function in older adults with Alzheimer's disease.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of six weeks of ankle stretching exercises on ankle dorsiflexion range of motion and anterior knee pain in children with ankle pronation: a randomized controlled trial
item.description: A six-week ankle stretching exercise program significantly improved ankle dorsiflexion range of motion and reduced anterior knee pain in children with ankle pronation.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Differences in the Thoracolumbar Fascia Between Low Back Pain Patients and Healthy Individuals: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found significant differences in the thoracolumbar fascia characteristics between individuals with low back pain and healthy controls.
item.author: Sports Med - Open

item.title: The effect of SportsMetrics training program on functional performance, landing error, dynamic knee valgus and hamstrings/quadriceps strength in athletes: a systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis confirmed the effectiveness of the SportsMetrics training program in improving functional performance, reducing landing errors, dynamic knee valgus, and enhancing hamstrings/quadriceps strength in athletes.
item.author: BMC Sports Sci Med Rehabil

item.title: Arm exercise training in chronic obstructive pulmonary disease: an umbrella review of systematic reviews and meta-analyses.
item.description: An umbrella review synthesized findings on arm exercise training for COPD patients, screening six databases to identify systematic reviews and meta-analyses to establish evidence levels for its effectiveness.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Development and psychometric validation of the shoulder problems assessment scale.
item.description: A 12-item Shoulder Problems Assessment Scale (SPAS) was developed and validated using a multicenter design (n=415) to provide an activity-based patient-reported outcome measure with a hierarchical stepwise yes/no format for identifying the first threshold of difficulty during daily activities.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Joint non-linear dose-response associations of device-measured physical activity and cardiorespiratory fitness with cardiovascular disease: a cohort and Mendelian randomisation study
item.description: A UK Biobank cohort study (n=93,026) and Mendelian randomization assessed the non-linear joint dose-response associations of accelerometer-measured moderate-to-vigorous physical activity (MVPA) and estimated cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) with incident cardiovascular disease (CVD) risk.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: More Than Just Arm Movement: Finger-Worn Accelerometers Provide a Valid and Sensitive Alternative to Wrist-Worn Accelerometers for Measuring Real-World Upper-Limb Performance in Stroke Survivors
item.description: A cross-sectional observational study (n=20) compared finger-worn and wrist-worn accelerometers, finding finger-worn accelerometers to be a valid and more sensitive alternative for measuring real-world upper-limb motor performance in stroke survivors.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: A systematic review of early neuroimaging and neurophysiological biomarkers for post-stroke mobility prognostication.
item.description: A systematic review identified early neuroimaging and neurophysiological biomarkers measured within 14 days post-stroke that predict mobility outcomes up to 24 months, with varying prognostic capacities across different statistical approaches.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effect of kinesiology taping on limb oedema in patients with severe hyper-dependency using shear-wave elastography: a randomized clinical trial.
item.description: A randomized clinical trial with 50 patients found that kinesiology taping at 25% tension significantly reduced the elastic coefficient of the dermis in limb oedema compared to 0% tension taping by day 9, as measured by shear-wave elastography.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of Fingertip Vibrotactile Stimulation on Postural Control in Community-Dwelling Older Adults: A Comparison Across Age Groups
item.description: Fingertip vibrotactile stimulation improved postural control, measured by center of pressure velocity and area, in 348 community-dwelling older adults across young-old (65-74), old-old (75-84), and oldest-old (≥85) age groups.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Effects of functional versus conventional Physiotherapy-Based pain management on symptoms, psychological outcomes, and quality of life in women with Bladder Pain Syndrome: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
item.description: This RCT (n=28) compared functional versus conventional physiotherapy in women with Bladder Pain Syndrome, finding no significant differences in symptom severity, psychological outcomes, or quality of life.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Experiences of telehealth e-mentoring within postgraduate musculoskeletal physical therapy education in Canada and the United Kingdom.
item.description: A qualitative study explored experiences of postgraduate Masters physiotherapy mentees and mentors engaged in telehealth e-mentoring in Canada and compared findings with the UK, identifying its potential for advanced practice capabilities.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Methodological characteristics of perturbation-based balance training in healthy older adults: A scoping review.
item.description: A scoping review mapped the methodological features of mechanically induced perturbation-based balance training interventions in healthy older adults, supporting its potential role in fall prevention but highlighting variability.
item.author: PubMed
